title: Release window harmonization and execution runbook for cross-surface launches
creator: Aisha Martinez
description:
Objective: Create a single, pragmatic runbook and harmonized launch-window coverage matrix for multi-surface (runtime, console, API) feature launches that reduces coordination friction, clarifies ownership, and enforces capacity gates and rollbacks. Scope: cross-team launches that touch hosted/runtime endpoints, console UX, and public API surface. Excludes purely internal infra hotfixes.

Goals and success metrics:
- 90% of coordinated launches use the runbook and coverage matrix by Q2.
- Reduce last-minute escalations due to capacity by 60% versus baseline.
- Mean time-to-safe-rollback during launch windows < 30 minutes in 90th percentile.

Constraints and trade-offs:
- We will favor deterministic, timeboxed windows over ad-hoc approvals for predictable SRE staffing, accepting slightly longer overall rollout times for lower operational churn.
- Automated gating (capacity-based) will be conservative initially to avoid false positives that block launches; tuning will follow real-world telemetry.
- One canonical runbook must remain lightweight (1–2 pages) with links to detailed checklists to avoid ceremony.

Stakeholders and roles:
- PM owner: Aisha Martinez (product orchestration lead)
- Release coordinator: Liam O'Connor (assignee)
- Runtime SREs: ENG-4123 team
- Console product/design: DES-198 + Console PMs
- API platform: ENG-4210
- Customer-facing comms: Growth & Support

Proposed components:
1) Coverage matrix: grid mapping launch windows to service owners, regional blackout windows, and required on-call coverage. Includes primary and secondary owners and p-staff contact.
2) Capacity gating policy: threshold definitions (CPU/GPU utilization, queue depth, tail latency) and action steps (hold, throttle, rollback).
3) Canary schedule template: timeboxed canary plan with traffic ramps, verification signals, and rollback triggers.
4) Communication templates: internal Slack runbook channel template, customer-facing incident/feature notes, and on-call escalation steps.
5) Cutover checklist: pre-cutover validations, dependency checks (DB migrations, schema flags), and rollback verification steps.
6) Post-mortem / telemetry tasks: capture launch metrics and quality regressions into Optimize evals and cost telemetry.

Implementation approach:
- Draft the runbook and matrix with runtime and console leads by 2026-03-05.
- Run two dry-run rehearsals (one at low-traffic time, one at high-traffic time) with canary and rollback paths.
- Iterate policy thresholds based on rehearsal telemetry.
- Bake runbook into the Console Launch flow (link to pre-launch checkbox) and into Release Calendar templates.

Risks and mitigations:
- Risk: over-conservative gates block launches. Mitigation: define explicit override path with SRE/PM signoff and automated audit logs.
- Risk: unfamiliarity across teams. Mitigation: 2x training sessions + runbook one-pagers + tabletop exercises.

Deliverables:
- 1-page canonical runbook + printable checklist (PDF)
- Coverage matrix spreadsheet with ownership and regional rows
- Canary schedule and traffic ramp templates in Confluence
- Integration tasks for Console pre-launch checklist and Release Calendar automation

Longer-term: integrate coverage matrix with automated on-call paging and capacity forecasting to recommend launch windows programmatically.
acceptance_criteria: Canonical runbook reviewed and approved by runtime SRE, console PM, and API platform lead
Coverage matrix populated for top 10 anticipated launches in next quarter
Two dry-run rehearsals executed and telemetry captured
Console pre-launch checklist includes link to the runbook and requires signoff from primary owners
Documented rollback and override process with audit logging
